chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus or someone else, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The wergild (blood money) of the foetus is five parts: one-fifth for the nutfah (seed/drop) is twenty dinars; and for the alaqah (clot) two-fifths is forty dinars; and for the mudghah (lump of flesh) three-fifths is sixty dinars; and for the 'idham (bones) four-fifths is eighty dinars. So when the foetus is complete, its wergild is one hundred dinars. So when the spirit is breathed into it, its wergild is one thousand dinars or ten thousand dirhams if it is a male; and if it is a female, then five hundred dinars. And if the woman is killed while she is pregnant, and it is not known whether her child was a male or a female, then the wergild of the child is two halves: half the wergild of the male and half the wergild of the female; and her wergild is complete.

key_terms.الْمُضْغَةُ: The lump of flesh stage of development

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a foetus at different stages of development in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the graduated scale of blood money (diyah) for a foetus, reflecting the Shia juristic view of progressive ensoulment and legal personhood from the nutfah stage to full birth. It establishes a clear distinction between male and female diyah once the soul is breathed in, while providing a pragmatic solution for uncertainty regarding the child's sex if the mother is killed, ensuring the mother's full compensation is preserved.
